replacements.old: For DFR, the partial *C. japonica* CjDFR clone `AB524885.1` (Tateishi et al., 2010) was compared with the six tea DFR-family reference candidates classified by Mei et al. (2019). Published CjDFR primer pairs, including the 167-bp assay of Larcher et al. (2015), were used as independent assay-to-sequence links. The white/pink tea source locus `CSA003949` from Zhou et al. (2020) was cross-walked to the tea DFR reference family before paralog classification. ANS/LDOX and ANR evidence was treated more conservatively because several source contrasts use reference-mapped or family-level features rather than deposited species-native orthologs. These analyses support copy-aware directional heterogeneity but were not interpreted as strict-node recurrence.
replacements.new: For DFR, the partial *C. japonica* CjDFR clone `AB524885.1` (Tateishi et al., 2010) was compared with the six tea DFR-family reference candidates classified by Mei et al. (2019). Published CjDFR primer pairs, including the 167-bp assay of Berruti et al. (2015), were used as independent assay-to-sequence links. The white/pink tea source locus `CSA003949` from Zhou et al. (2020) was cross-walked to the tea DFR reference family before paralog classification. ANS/LDOX and ANR evidence was treated more conservatively because several source contrasts use reference-mapped or family-level features rather than deposited species-native orthologs (Geng et al., 2022; Qu et al., 2024). These analyses support copy-aware directional heterogeneity but were not interpreted as strict-node recurrence.

replacements.old: The pollination synthesis likewise showed that visible hue was not a deterministic reproductive-function state. Primary evidence included contrasting broad pollinator functions within the same visible colour, and pollination weighting could change with season, weather, or disturbance without a visible-hue change (Kunitake et al., 2004; Abe et al., 2013; Sun et al., 2017; Mori et al., 2023; Zhang et al., 2024; Jiang et al., 2025). After updating *C. oleifera* with direct bird-exclusion evidence from the same study that documented pollen toxicity (Zhang et al., 2024), the count-preserving hue–pollinator-function association remained weak in the small evidence seed (*P* = 0.77127). This result was not interpreted as evidence of independence; instead, it indicated that coarse A/W/Y labels are insufficient to represent the full sensory, reward, and reproductive phenotype relevant to ecological filtering.

After updating *C. oleifera* with direct bird-exclusion evidence from the same study that documented pollen toxicity (Zhang et al., 2024), the count-preserving hue–pollinator-function association remained weak in the small evidence seed (*P* = 0.77127). This result was not interpreted as evidence of independence; instead, it indicated that coarse A/W/Y labels are insufficient to represent the full sensory, reward, and reproductive phenotype relevant to ecological filtering.
